variants.title: SQUID magnetometry: blocking of magnetite nanoparticles
variants.sample: Magnetite nanoparticles, 10 nm, dilute in a matrix (SIMULATED)
variants.method: M-H loop at 5 K and ZFC-FC M-T in 0.1 mT
variants.note: Monodisperse single-domain particles (Bean-Livingston): ZFC and FC agree above the blocking temperature TB = KV/(kB ln(tm/tau0)) and part below it; the FC curve freezes at its value at TB, so TB = (m T at high temperature)/(FC plateau). Ms = 480 kA/m and K = 16 kJ/m^3 are magnetite-like values quoted from memory - verify; the size and number are illustrative.

source.title: C. P. Bean and J. D. Livingston, J. Appl. Phys. 30, 120S (1959); magnetite Ms and K quoted from memory - verify

variants.title: SQUID magnetometry: Meissner signal of a niobium sphere
variants.sample: Niobium sphere of 1 mm^3, Tc 9.25 K (SIMULATED)
variants.method: M-H at 2 K and ZFC-FC M-T in 1 mT
variants.unknown: diamagnetic moment against field, Tc from the ZFC shielding
variants.note: Zero-field cooled, the sphere shields its whole volume (m = -3/2 V B/mu0, demagnetising factor of a sphere); field cooled it expels only part of the flux. The shielding fraction 1 - (T/Tc)^4 is an illustrative two-fluid form; the ZFC moment against T^4 is a line that reaches zero at Tc. Tc of niobium 9.25 K (Kittel).

source.title: C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, Table 10.1: Nb Tc = 9.25 K
